blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Referring expression grounding in overhead imagery requires oriented bounding boxes rather than horizontal ones, since aerial objects appear at arbitrary orientations. Most grounding models emit box coordinates sequentially; Parallel Box Decoding (PBD) instead predicts all geometry slots in one forward pass, but only for four-coordinate horizontal boxes. We extend this block-aligned interface to a six-slot oriented representation using a double-angle parameterization. Rather than assuming correctness from a decreasing loss curve, we verify the extension with image/prompt-shuffle controls and visibility/leakage probes, which show that the corrected model depends on both the image and the prompt rather than on prompt statistics alone. On the aerial vehicle visual grounding (AVVG) benchmark, whose targets are genuinely oriented, the extended model improves rotated intersection over union (rotIoU) from 0.1253 for the zero-shot baseline to 0.303 +/- 0.012 (mean +/- standard deviation over three training seeds) across the complete 6139-record test split spanning all 120 images. Learning oriented boxes rather than their axis-aligned envelopes adds 0.055 +/- 0.008 rotIoU beyond a matched control (per-seed 95% confidence intervals all excluding zero), whereas block expansion alone yields no rotIoU gain distinguishable from zero.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Referring expression grounding—localizing the object referred to by a natural-language expression—has been
studied extensively on natural images ( Kamath et al., 2021 ; Li et al., 2022 ) , and increasingly on remote-sensing and
unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery ( Zhan et al., 2023 ; Kuckreja et al., 2024 ; Zhou et al., 2024 ) . The remote-sensing setting is harder for
reasons largely absent from natural-image benchmarks: scenes are dense with many similar objects (rows of
vehicles, repeated structures), targets are small relative to the image, and referring expressions often depend
on relational or comparative language (“the car closest to the camera”) that cannot be resolved from box
geometry alone. A further difficulty specific to overhead imagery is that objects appear at arbitrary in-plane
orientations. A horizontal bounding box (HBB), the output format most grounding systems still use, fits an
elongated, rotated object poorly, as the aerial-detection literature has documented at length ( Xia et al., 2018 ; Xie et al., 2021 ) . An oriented bounding box (OBB), parameterized by center, size, and orientation, is the natural alternative when the referred object has a meaningful aspect ratio and heading.

blocks.en:
Most vision-language grounding models emit box coordinates as autoregressively generated tokens, one coordinate
at a time. This costs one decoding step per coordinate and treats a geometrically atomic quantity—one box—as
an arbitrarily ordered token sequence. LocateAnything ( Wang et al., 2026 ) addresses this with Parallel Box Decoding (PBD): a block-aligned interface in which a trigger token is followed by a
single forward pass that predicts every coordinate slot together, rather than one token at a time. This is
faster and keeps the coordinate representation aligned with the geometric unit it describes, but the released
formulation covers only four-coordinate horizontal boxes. Whether this block-aligned interface extends to a
six-slot oriented representation—and what computational and accuracy trade-offs that extension entails—was not examined by the original method and is the main focus of this study. Separately, joint-regression
architectures such as SATGround ( Toker et al., 2025 ) predict OBB parameters with a dedicated regression head
rather than a coordinate-token interface. This is a different architectural design from the block-aligned
decoding extended here, and the two are not compared head-to-head in this study (Section 5.2 ).

blocks.en:
Extending the PBD interface from four coordinates to six is not merely a matter of changing a configuration
value. The block-alignment guarantee of PBD—that coordinate slots see the image and prompt through an intact
causal prefix—can fail silently: in the pretrained backbone’s training path, the coordinate slots lost
visibility of the image and prompt while the training loss still decreased normally. Such a failure is invisible
in a loss curve and was found only with targeted diagnostic probes (Section 3.3 ), which is
why this study treats verification of the extension as part of the method rather than as an afterthought.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: 2.1 Visual Grounding on Natural Images
blocks.zh: 2.1 自然图像的视觉地基

blocks.en:
Visual grounding—localizing the object referred to by a natural-language expression—has mostly been
studied as text-conditioned detection on natural images. The task originates from crowd-sourced
referring-expression benchmarks such as ReferItGame ( Kazemzadeh et al., 2014 ) and the RefCOCO,
RefCOCO+, and RefCOCOg splits ( Yu et al., 2016 ; Mao et al., 2016 ) , which pair a natural-language description
with a single target region in everyday photographs. The detection transformer (DETR) ( Carion et al., 2020 ) later provided an end-to-end, set-prediction backbone that grounding-specific models build
on. Modulated DETR (MDETR) ( Kamath et al., 2021 ) trains an end-to-end detector on aligned text-image pairs, jointly reasoning
over phrases and image regions to support both phrase grounding and referring expression comprehension. Grounded language-image pretraining (GLIP) ( Li et al., 2022 ) unifies object detection and phrase grounding as a single grounded pretraining objective at
scale, showing that a shared text-image formulation transfers across detection and grounding benchmarks. More
recent open-vocabulary detectors and multimodal large language models extend this lineage further: Grounding DINO ( Liu et al., 2024 ) combines a DETR-style detector with grounded pretraining for open-set detection,
while Kosmos-2 ( Peng et al., 2024 ) , Shikra ( Chen et al., 2023 ) , and Ferret ( You et al., 2024 ) equip
general-purpose vision-language models with coordinate grounding by representing boxes or points as tokens or
continuous features the language model can emit or consume. All of the above establish the text-conditioned
detection lineage that remote-sensing grounding methods build on, but none addresses oriented geometry or a
parallel, block-aligned coordinate decoder.

blocks.en: 2.2 Remote-Sensing Visual Grounding
blocks.zh: 2.2 遥感视地

blocks.en:
Remote-sensing visual grounding (RSVG) adapts the grounding problem to aerial and satellite imagery, where small
targets, dense scenes, and orientation variation make localization substantially harder than in natural images.
RSVG ( Zhan et al., 2023 ) defines the task with image-expression-box triplets on DIOR-RSVG using horizontal
bounding boxes, starting the remote-sensing grounding benchmark lineage without oriented annotations. Later remote-sensing vision-language models add oriented or multi-format grounding: GeoChat ( Kuckreja et al., 2024 ) is a region-level dialogue model whose remote-sensing setting includes oriented
annotations, and GeoGround ( Zhou et al., 2024 ) unifies horizontal-box, oriented-box, and mask grounding in
one model, introducing the RefGeo instruction-following collection this study’s AVVG subset is drawn from.
GeoChat and GeoGround therefore already demonstrate that oriented-box remote-sensing grounding is achievable.

blocks.en: 2.3 Oriented Object Detection in Aerial Imagery
blocks.zh: 2.3 空中图像中定向物体探测

blocks.en:
A parallel line of work treats oriented bounding boxes as a detection-geometry problem rather than a
language-grounding one. DOTA ( Xia et al., 2018 ) established a large-scale aerial object detection benchmark with
quadrilateral annotations, motivating oriented representations by documenting the scale, orientation, and aspect-ratio variation that horizontal boxes fail to capture in aerial scenes; FAIR1M ( Sun et al., 2022 ) and
HRSC2016 ( Liu et al., 2017 ) extend this benchmark lineage to fine-grained category labels and ship-specific
imagery, respectively, each also using oriented annotations. A large family of detectors builds directly on these
benchmarks: the region-of-interest (RoI) Transformer ( Ding et al., 2019 ) learns a spatial transformation of region proposals
under OBB supervision, Gliding Vertex ( Xu et al., 2021 ) regresses relative vertex offsets on a
horizontal box instead of an angle, S 2 A-Net ( Han et al., 2022 ) aligns convolutional features to refined
oriented anchors, ReDet ( Han et al., 2021 ) incorporates rotation-equivariant backbone features, and Oriented
R-CNN ( Xie et al., 2021 ) is a representative high-performance detector built directly around oriented
proposals and regression. A separate line of work addresses the angle-regression discontinuity directly; the same
discontinuity motivates this study’s double-angle parameterization (Section 3.1 ). SCRDet ( Yang et al., 2019 ) adds an IoU-smooth L1 loss, which uses the intersection over union (IoU) between boxes to reduce the loss
discontinuity near the periodic boundary,
circular smooth label ( Yang and Yan, 2020 ) recasts angle regression as classification over discretized bins, and the Kullback–Leibler divergence (KLD) ( Yang et al., 2021a ) and Gaussian Wasserstein distance (GWD) ( Yang et al., 2021b ) losses instead convert the rotated box into a Gaussian
distribution and regress a distribution distance that is well behaved at the periodic boundary. None of these
methods is a text-conditioned grounding system. They motivate the oriented-geometry problem that this study
addresses within a language-grounding model rather than a closed-set detector, and their reported metrics (mean average precision, mAP, under detection-style matching) are not directly comparable to the rotated-IoU grounding protocol used here.

blocks.en: 2.4 Structured and Parallel Coordinate Decoding
blocks.zh: 2.4 结构化和平行坐标解码

blocks.en:
Representing structured outputs as token sequences is a broader trend: Pix2Seq ( Chen et al., 2022 ) casts object detection as language modeling over a serialized sequence of quantized box-and-class tokens, and OFA ( Wang et al., 2022 ) unifies captioning, grounding, and other vision-language tasks under the same
sequence-to-sequence interface. Both, like the grounding models discussed above, decode one token at a time. Two
lines of prior work instead pursue non-autoregressive or partially parallel decoding: in machine translation,
non-autoregressive neural machine translation ( Gu et al., 2018 ) produces all output tokens in a single forward
pass at some cost in output quality, and in object detection, Deformable DETR ( Zhu et al., 2021 ) predicts a fixed set of object queries in parallel through cross-attention to deformable sampling points rather
than a serialized coordinate sequence. Most vision-language grounding models, however, still emit box coordinates
as a sequence of autoregressively generated tokens, one coordinate at a time. LocateAnything ( Wang et al., 2026 ) instead introduces Parallel Box Decoding (PBD), treating a box as a single
structured unit whose geometry slots are predicted together in one block-aligned forward pass rather than in four sequential token predictions. LocateAnything’s released formulation covers four-coordinate horizontal boxes;
it does not report an oriented extension or the angle-prediction behavior that orientation
introduces into the same block-aligned interface. This is the method that the present work extends.
Separately, SATGround ( Toker et al., 2025 ) interfaces a remote-sensing grounding module through specialized
localization control tokens on a fine-tuned vision-language model, jointly reasoning over language and spatial information to
regress oriented box geometry. Because a joint OBB regression head of this kind already exists in the
remote-sensing grounding literature, this study’s contribution is specifically the PBD coordinate-block mechanism,
not joint OBB regression as such. This study does not compare against SATGround head-to-head under a matched
protocol; see the scope note in Section 5.2 .

Because a block-alignment failure can corrupt training without appearing in the loss curve, the six-slot
extension was validated with the diagnostic probes of Section 3.6 before any performance
metric was reported. One finding matters for the method: in the backbone’s training path, the causal-prefix
length that should expose the image and prompt tokens to the coordinate slots was computed from a position-ID
pattern that training never produces, so the coordinate slots saw none of the image or prompt tokens while the

and the visibility probe confirms the fix: on the same training batch, the first coordinate slot’s attention
mask goes from 7 of 894 keys, none of them image or prompt tokens, to all 894.
Four further defects in the backbone code caused outright failures (crashes) rather than silent ones; they are
also corrected and are listed in Appendix A , and the source changes are available as described in
the Data Availability Statement.

blocks.en:
We evaluate with the direct PBD decoder, which constructs the prompt, the <box> token, and six coordinate
mask slots and obtains the geometry logits in a single forward pass. This path matches the training block
definition. The upstream generate() path implements multi-token prediction only for the original
six-token HBB block, so the six-slot model is evaluated through the direct decoder.

定义。 上游生成( ) 路径只为原始执行多键预测

The primary metric is rotated IoU (rotIoU): the IoU between the predicted and ground-truth oriented boxes,
computed from the polygon intersection of the two oriented quadrilaterals using the Shapely library (version 2.1.2) rather than
a custom clipping routine. We also report axis-aligned IoU (aabbIoU), the IoU between the HBB envelopes (defined
below) of the predicted and ground-truth boxes, which compares with the original HBB baseline on its own terms.
The remaining metrics are threshold accuracies at
rotIoU 0.50 and 0.75 (Acc@0.50, Acc@0.75), angle mean absolute error (MAE) in degrees, and the decoded percentage.
A decoding failure is assigned zero IoU and is included in the denominator.

rotIoU 0.50和 0.75(Acc@0.50,Acc@0.75),角度指度的绝对出错(MAE)和已解码的百分比.
解码失败被指定为0 IoU并包含在分母中.

The baseline is the zero-shot LocateAnything-3B backbone evaluated with its upstream generate() path on
the complete AVVG test split, and serves as the primary HBB baseline. We define the HBB envelope of a box
as the tightest axis-aligned rectangle enclosing it. A reference derived from the ground truth (GT), the GT-derived HBB envelope (reference) —the HBB envelope of each target’s GT oriented box—is reported

computed reference point that illustrates the gap between horizontal and oriented representations, but it is not
guaranteed to be the rotIoU- maximizing axis-aligned rectangle for each target, so its score should be read
as a reference value rather than as a formal upper bound on what any axis-aligned prediction could achieve
(Section 4.1 ).

blocks.en: We use three complementary checks beyond the main score:

1. Image dependence: evaluate each selected checkpoint with matched image/prompt pairs,
independently shuffled images, and independently shuffled prompts (Section 4.3 ). A  large matched-versus-image-shuffled gap is required before treating the score as evidence that the
coordinate slots use visual input. This check is motivated by the broader concern that a high grounding
score need not demonstrate use of every required input modality: Cirik et al. (2018) show that a
system given only the image, with the referring expression withheld, still reaches 71.2% top-2 precision
on a standard benchmark, indicating that the benchmark’s own label distribution—not language
understanding—accounts for much of that score. Their ablation tests dependence on language; the image-shuffled
condition here tests the complementary case, dependence on vision. 2. Implementation visibility and leakage probes: verify that coordinate slots can attend to the
image and that ground-truth coordinate tokens are not injected into the model input during training. 3. Qualitative overlays: render predictions and target OBBs on the original UAV frames to
distinguish geometric errors from referring failures, such as placing a box on a neighboring vehicle
(Figure 2 ).

blocks.en: 4.2 HBB-Envelope Control: Isolating the Format-Switch Effect from the Orientation-Learning Effect
blocks.zh: 4.2 六溴代二苯-信封控制:将格式-开关效应从方向学习效应中分离出来

blocks.en:
The improvement in Table 2 could in principle come from the six-slot block format itself
rather than from learning to predict orientation. To separate these two effects, we trained a control arm with a
recipe identical to the reported model—the same block size, six-slot collator, loss weights, and LoRA targets—except that the training target is the axis-aligned envelope of the ground-truth polygon, so its orientation
is structurally fixed to 0 ∘ 0^{\circ} / 90 ∘ 90^{\circ} . Ground truth for scoring remains the original oriented box in
both arms, so this control isolates the format-switch effect from the orientation-learning effect without changing
the evaluation. Because a tilted target’s envelope is larger than its oriented box, the orientation-learning step
necessarily compares learning the oriented box with learning its larger envelope; part of its gain is the tighter
extent that representing orientation permits, which cannot be separated from orientation itself. A third arm,
HBB-PBD, separates the two-slot expansion from the effect of adapting to AVVG itself: it keeps the original
upstream four-slot corner block
( <box> x1 y1 x2 y2 </box> , block_size = 6 ) rather than the six-slot block, fine-tuned on the
same subset with the same axis-aligned envelope target as the HBB-envelope control. All three arms are trained
with the same three seeds and use the same validation-disjoint checkpoint-selection protocol
(Section 3.5 ); the selected epoch is 5 in eight of the nine trained runs and 4 for
OBB-PBD seed 3, whose validation rotIoU plateaued between epochs 4 and 5. HBB-PBD’s evaluation does not exclude
corner-touching targets: the four-slot format cannot represent
axis-aligned envelopes that touch a corner of the resized image (about 4% of this test split), and those cases
are scored as ordinary decode failures (IoU 0) rather than excluded, so this arm is evaluated on the same test records as
every row of Table 2 . Its own training set is nonetheless about 10.3% smaller
than the HBB-envelope control’s and the main model’s (20,182 vs. 22,495 AVVG training records), because the
same corner-frame constraint that is tolerated as a decode failure at test time was applied as an exclusion
filter at train time; this arm’s numbers should be read with that training-data asymmetry in mind.

blocks.zh: 4.4 结果的效率和局限性

blocks.en:
Latency is measured on a single GPU (NVIDIA RTX 6000 Ada, 48 GB) at batch size one over 60 test samples. The six-slot rows use the OBB-PBD seed-1 checkpoint (Table 6 ); the four-slot row uses the base
weights in the upstream four-slot layout, since latency depends on the block configuration rather than on the

latency from 306.87 ms to 329.82 ms (median 306.58 ms and 329.77 ms, 95th
percentile 309.45 ms and 332.57 ms), a 1.075 × 1.075\times ratio—a modest slot-expansion overhead.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusions
blocks.zh: 6. 结论

blocks.en:
This paper extends LocateAnything’s Parallel Box Decoding interface from a four-coordinate horizontal box to a
six-slot oriented box and reports what the extension costs and gains under a diagnostic evaluation protocol.
Diagnostic probes exposed a backbone defect that let the training loss decrease while the coordinate slots could
not see the image, and verified its correction; shuffle controls and visibility/leakage probes check the reported
decoding path throughout. Under this protocol, and across three training seeds, the extension improves rotIoU over
the zero-shot baseline on the complete AVVG test split, with checkpoint selection kept disjoint from that split
(Section 3.5 ). Matched control arms isolate how much of this gain comes from learning the
oriented box rather than from the larger coordinate block alone (Section 4.2 ).

blocks.en:
Two methodological directions follow directly from what this study leaves open. First, future work should
validate the loss weights in Table 1 through multi-seed, equal-budget ablations of the
reported five-epoch configuration. Second, a matched-protocol comparison with localization-token/MLP
joint-regression architectures such as SATGround ( Toker et al., 2025 ) (Section 5.2 ) would
quantify how coordinate-token decoding and dedicated regression heads differ in accuracy, decoded percentage,
and inference cost. Beyond these, extending the validated protocol to remote-sensing settings outside
the AVVG/UAV data studied here—different sensors, object scales, or grounding annotation formats—remains untested and
is not claimed here.

直接从本研究留下的内容中得出两个方法方向。 第一,今后的工作应当
